title: How Ankit Pathak Built a 1,000+ Person AI Consulting Empire (From Trainee to CEO)
text:
Ankit Pathak is the CEO of ConsultAdd Inc, an IT consulting and AI solutions company with over 1,000 employees and offices across the U.S. and India. Starting as a marketing trainee, Ankit built one of the fastest-growing AI-driven consulting firms by focusing on solving real problems, not selling services.

In this episode, we go deep into how he scaled from 5 to 1,000+ people, how AI transformed his company’s GTM and RevOps, and why he believes in “AI augmenting humans, not replacing them.”

Ankit shares actionable insights on market positioning, lead generation, consultative sales, ecosystem partnerships, and the mindset shift required to scale a global AI consulting business.
We also explore his creative side - from poetry to sneaker collecting - and how empathy and creativity shape his leadership style.

Here’s what you’ll learn:
[00:00] - Introduction Ankit Pathak
[01:10] - How ConsultAdd Inc Found Its Niche and Scaled with AI Solutions
[03:00] - “Don’t Pitch, Show Results” - How Prototypes Won Their First Clients
[07:30] - Using AI Agents for Personalized Outreach & Lead Generation
[10:30] - Building Trust and Relationships through Roundtables & Ecosystem Partnerships
[14:33] - Consultative Sales: Listening, Prototyping, and Solving Problems Fast
[22:05] - How RevOps & “Time to Value” Became Their North Star Metric
[24:42] - Customer Success Philosophy: Trust, Time-to-Value & Expansion
[28:20] - Flat Structure, Culture, and Leading Teams Across the U.S. & India
[33:07] - From Marketing Trainee to CEO of a 1,000+ Person Consulting Firm
[34:57] - How Poetry Shapes Leadership & Empathy
[38:00] - Sneaker Collecting, Creativity, and Staying Balanced as a CEO

title: AI GTM Consultant — Automated Go-To-Market Strategy & Analysis
channelName: Alpine Systems - The AI SaaS Factory
text:
The Problem:  Most GTM strategies are built on gut feel or outdated spreadsheets. Hiring a top-tier GTM consultant costs $20k+ a month, making high-level strategic analysis inaccessible for many growing companies.

The Solution:  I built the AI GTM Consultant—a Go-To-Market expert version of my SaaS logic engine. It analyzes your market position, identifies revenue leaks, and builds a readiness roadmap based on real GTM frameworks.

Strategic Capabilities:

Market Readiness: Instantly assesses if your product-market fit (PMF) signals are strong enough to scale.

Revenue Architecture: Identifies the "suck" in your current funnel and suggests automation fixes.

Strategic Roadmap: Generates actionable GTM plays that usually take weeks of manual consulting to produce.

The Tech Stack:  This is a high-reasoning build from the SaaS Factory:

Claude Code (The Strategic "Brain")

Supabase (Client Data & Persistent Logic)

Vercel (The Executive Dashboard)

The "Entry Wedge": This tool is often the first step in how I help businesses. We use the AI to find the gaps, and then we build the custom tools to close them.

GLM 5.2 is a free, open-source model that often beats Claude on everyday work, yet companies still pay frontier prices. The real bottleneck is no longer the model call. It is the last mile around it: context, routing, and harnesses.

My Links 🔗
👉🏻 Newsletter: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/

👉🏻 TikTok:   / nate.b.jones

What's really happening when intelligence gets 98% cheaper but your company's context stays trapped?

The common story is that a cheaper, better model means you should switch, but the real question is whether you can move your context, not whether the model can answer your prompt.

In this video, I share the inside scoop on GLM 5.2 and the last mile of cheap AI:

Where GLM 5.2 can safely replace an expensive frontier model
Why switching models means replacing a whole work system, not a call
How Claude Tag turns your team's Slack context into a sticky harness
What builders and agencies can do to own the last mile

Cheap intelligence is real and it is here, but the edge in 2026 belongs to whoever can build the harness and keep their own context instead of renting it back from a frontier lab.
